issues.claim: mid_market: "Retainers: $250-$2,500/mo (NJ AI Automation $250-$1,000; TwoCore $500-$1,500; Automaly from $2,500; SuperDupr states $200-$2,000 a month for support and monitoring)"
issues.problem: Every figure inside the parenthesis is confirmed verbatim on the vendor pages, but the band's stated floor ($250) sits above SuperDupr's published $200 floor quoted in the same sentence, so the band excludes a sourced data point it lists. It is labeled as a grouping in inference_note, so this is an internal consistency nit rather than an unsupported price.
issues.fix: Write the band as "about $200-$2,500/mo" (SuperDupr $200-$2,000; NJ AI Automation $250-$1,000; TwoCore $500-$1,500; Automaly fractional AI lead from $2,500), or drop SuperDupr's range from that sentence and keep it only in the band derivation. The one_line's "about $250-$2,500/mo" should match whichever form is chosen.

issues.claim: implications_for_consultancy[1]: "Buyers in this segment already accept a paid, credited audit at $497-$1,900, with $6,500 the top of the published range."
issues.problem: The $497-$1,900 lower span is confirmed (MapScale $497 in prose, NJ AI $500, OVAMIND $500, HA $1,200, Agentomte $1,900), but "$6,500 the top of the published range" is overstated against the brief's own sourced set: LuMay publishes a Discovery Sprint at $10K-$15K (lumay.ai/pricing) and AgenticIndex puts the median one-time entry for Fractional AI Advisory at $4,500 (n=13). It is labeled [Inference], so it is not presented as fact, but the superlative is not supported.
issues.fix: Reword to "with credited assessments clustering at $497-$1,900 and Automaly's at $6,500" and, if a ceiling is needed, note that discovery-type products in the same set run higher (LuMay $10K-$15K discovery sprint; AgenticIndex fractional-advisory median one-time entry $4,500, n=13).

issues.problem: The page's own body text says the figures "come from the pricing pages of 13 agencies, checked on 23 October 2026, and ours", while its section heading says "What 14 agencies publish" (13 + AI Strike Force itself = 14 rows). The brief's count follows the heading, so nothing is misquoted, but the source is self-inconsistent.
issues.fix: Call it "AI Strike Force's 13-agency comparison (plus its own row), checked 23 October 2026" and keep the existing note that AI Strike Force appears in its own table.

issues.claim: caveats: "The Reddit and Indie Hackers items come from thread titles as returned in search results"
issues.problem: Too pessimistic about the Indie Hackers item: the specifics in buyer_complaints (a $2,500/month client, three days of downtime, roughly 40 missed leads) do appear in the search-engine summary of the post, not just in its title. Direct fetch returns HTTP 403 for both, as the brief says.
issues.fix: Say the two items could not be opened directly (403) and were read from search-result summaries of the posts, with the specifics drawn from the summary of the Indie Hackers post rather than its title.

issues.claim: buyer_reported_costs heading as a whole (Streamline IQ case study, Wealthy Tent write-up)
issues.problem: Neither source reports what a buyer said; both are seller-side or writer-side accounts. The brief states this in each item's context and in caveats, so nothing is misrepresented as buyer testimony, but the section label invites the opposite reading.
issues.fix: Retitle the section "reported deal prices (seller- or third-party-reported)" or prefix each finding with "[Seller-reported]" so the label does not overstate who is speaking.
